correctness.rationale: On the 2π-periodic torus with normalized Haar measure and mean-zero H² domain, the normal constant-coefficient generator acts diagonally on e^{i(px+qy)} with squared modulus (p²+q²)²+a²(p+αq)²; changing q sign yields equation (5). Fibonacci pairs satisfy F_{n−1}−αF_n=(−1)^nφ^(−n), giving a witness O(a^(4/3)). Every minimizing frequency for large a has |p−αq|<1/2, q≠0 and p nearest αq. In each interval F_n≤q<F_{n+1}, the adjacent-convergent unimodular basis and sign inequalities for its integer coefficients give |p−αq|≥φ^(−n); monotonicity of nearest integer gives p≥F_{n−1}; hence BOTH nonnegative terms are minimized by the Fibonacci vector. Binet expansion yields Aφ^(4n)(1+O(φ^(−2n))); with a=φ^(3N)s, uniform exclusion of large ±j on compact s intervals makes the normalized minima converge uniformly to H(s)=min_j f(φ^j s^(−1/3)). Its period φ³, nonconstancy, sharp min f(x*) and max f(xc) follow from monotonicity on a single geometric-lattice cell. Independent exact/high-precision bounded arithmetic checked 33 denominator intervals, eight global finite Fourier minima with certified quartic-radius truncations, phase periodicity and numerical constants. The finite checks support, but are not substitutes for, the unrestricted analytic proof. The average-relaxation consequence is Θ(a^(−2/3)), NOT a sharp prefactor, and ordinary semigroup relaxation stays unchanged.
